dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: Locally retained HD-EPIC research clip. Original-video identity and annotation provenance are preserved; this screening record does not grant redistribution rights.

original_annotations: P05-20240427-145526-60 [146.90, 147.83]: Pick up a different spoon with my right hand, I want a stainless steel one.

observed_events.description: The wearer moves a white chopping board near the sink and microwave, then turns toward the cutlery drawer below the counter.
The wearer opens the blue-fronted drawer. Separate compartments contain knives, forks and spoons; the hands do not initially hold eating utensils.

The right hand selects from the spoon compartments, brings an oval-bowled eating spoon out and transfers it to the left hand. A spoon is visibly held before the right hand reaches the fork compartment. Further hand movements among the spoons do not establish a material change or a discarded first spoon.

With a spoon still visible in the left hand, the right hand reaches into the fork compartment and lifts a fork. The spoon and the fork are simultaneously visible, with their different working shapes distinguishable.
The wearer brings the utensils together, continues handling cutlery and then moves away from the drawer with the gathered utensils. This is not a visible abandonment of the spoon category.
The wearer turns to the lower cabinet, takes a plate and moves toward another counter.

visual_review.annotation_limit: The narrated preference for stainless steel is not a visually established material fact. The clip supports spoon-before-fork category order, not a shopping-goal update or a material-based replacement.

unsupported_claims: The first spoon has a different material from a later spoon, or a spoon is discarded because of its material.
The filmed cutlery is confirmed stainless steel rather than another silver-coloured material.
The exact brand, model, measured size, alloy, commercial pack count, or retail product identity is visible.
The wearer abandons the spoon category, prefers forks to spoons, or changes a shopping goal in the source video.
The number of physical utensils taken from the drawer dictates the number of retail packs to buy.

prior_rejections.rejection_reason: The continuous sequence proves that a different packaged ingredient is used later, but the released V1 pixels show only an open blue tin and pale contents. The label is unreadable, so identifying it as coconut milk and linking it to the coconut-milk tutorial requires the HD-EPIC narration rather than visual evidence.

screening_lineage.visual_interpretation: The narration-mined material-change hypothesis is not used. This construction uses the independently inspected cutlery-selection event at 138-158 seconds, where spoon-before-fork order is visually grounded. The prior rejection concerned a different event at 235-265 seconds in the same original video and remains unchanged.

supported_claims.text: The initial drawer interaction is in the spoon compartments; an oval-bowled eating spoon is then held outside the drawer before the wearer reaches into the fork compartment.
The later drawer interaction brings out a fork while the spoon is still in the other hand. The spoon bowl and fork head distinguish the two utensil categories.
The ordered packet binds the first kind to eating spoons and the other kind to eating forks. A later still containing both types does not by itself establish which was taken first.

construct.research_question: Can the Agent remove a cancelled later utensil category while preserving a still-required earlier category from a visually grounded two-item cart?
construct.belief_before: A requires one qualifying spoon-only pack and one qualifying fork-only pack, because the source shows the wearer taking out those two eating-utensil types.
construct.belief_after: B cancels the second category and preserves the first category. The final cart requires one qualifying spoon-only pack and no fork pack; the original finish, material, minimum pack size and separate-pack constraints still apply.
construct.required_behavior_change: Remove the fork pack if already added, or omit it if not yet added, while retaining or completing exactly one qualifying spoon pack.
construct.no_update_failure: The fork pack remains in the final cart alongside the spoon pack after the user has cancelled the later category.
construct.overupdate_failure: The Agent removes the still-required spoon pack, retains only the fork pack, empties both goals, adds duplicates, or discards the unchanged material and packaging constraints.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: Neither A nor B names spoon or fork. The frames provide those categories and their action order; B alone supplies the cancellation. A final still with both utensils cannot recover first-kind order, and removing B leaves both packs required.

requirement_partition.source_grounded: Two eating-utensil categories are retrieved from the drawer, first a spoon and then a fork.
requirement_partition.authored_requirement: Plain silver-coloured stainless steel, no patterned or coloured handles, at least six pieces per pack, one separate single-type pack for each requested category, and the later cancellation of the second category are user requirements, not properties or intentions inferred from the video.
requirement_partition.website_grounded: The two captured Amazon result windows and their public product images support 22 qualifying spoon-pack ASINs and eight qualifying fork-pack ASINs. Index bindings and all 30 actual catalog images have been checked. The eight previously flagged accepted spoon titles now match rich canonical snapshots; the seven other generic window titles were repaired on 2026-09-14. Overall task semantic admission remains pending.

observed.why: These roles are possible task goal states, not a claim that the visible utensil is ambiguous. The user update, not the video, chooses between the two-item and reduced goals.

The fixed update keeps only the first kind taken out and excludes the other kind. The ordered source binds these roles to spoons retained and forks cancelled; unchanged purchasing constraints remain in force.

Upstream evidence supports 22 spoon-pack equivalents and eight fork-pack equivalents without adding video-unproved size, material or exact-product requirements.
semantic_review.current_mock_core_review: Only the four named core rejection records are accepted: each currently has a meaningful complete Mock title and a matching catalog image supporting its stated independent failure predicate. This limited per-entity approval is not acceptance of the whole task or Mock evidence loop.
notes: All fifteen previously flagged catalog titles now match meaningful canonical product snapshots: eight accepted spoon entries were already repaired, and seven remaining window entries were repaired on 2026-09-14. Overall task-level blind reconstruction and adversarial review remain pending.

All 22 final spoon answers are excluded from every negative ring. The eight qualifying fork packs are related final-state negatives only after B; buying one of them under A is valid work, not an initial mistake.

Simple continuous handle edging remains admissible. Repeated hammered, pearled or etched ornament is treated as a pattern. No unrequested exact dimension, spoon-bowl shape, brand, alloy grade or mirror-only finish is added.

A requires one pack from each category, giving 176 equivalent initial combinations. B preserves the same 22 spoon alternatives and removes only the fork commitment. Full lifecycle, behavioral and release acceptance have not been established.
